title: Invest....(but where?). Everything is falling: Gold, Nifty, AI Stocks
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions (English captions as fetched; auto-caption garbles noted where they affect numbers).
summary: Akshat Shrivastava's volatility playbook for a world where, since 2020, familiar refuges have stopped behaving as expected: wars and shocks have at times lifted US markets while Indian markets fell, and gold chasers were hurt when gold dropped after its run. His first two basics are diversification — spread money across Indian equities, US equities, gold and real estate rather than holding only Indian stocks, so a currency or local crisis is partly offset — and never chasing a running cycle; instead buy at consolidation/support points, the rectangular zones where an asset repeatedly finds buyers. Applied to gold, he says the metal is at support now and he is topping up 'a little bit', while warning it need not run from tomorrow. His main worked example is Google: down about 10% pre-market to support and roughly 30% from its peak, trading at a forward PE under 18, cheaper than Nifty 50, and already profitable in his portfolio, so it is a buy-on-dips stock held at 5-10% of the portfolio and added to at supports. He stresses broken price versus broken business — Kodak was a broken business that failed to innovate, while Google's fall reflects heavier AI capex (caption garbles the capex figures as '20 units' raised to '25 units'), not broken revenues — and warns AI disruption is a genuine threat to TCS and Infosys, where a broken-business case can at least be made. He then contrasts cyclical breakdowns (Nifty's flat 2007-2014 stretch during the global financial crisis) with structural ones, suggesting Nifty's roughly two to three years of zero returns while Japan, the UK, the US, Korea and Taiwan rose may be structural; he is cutting his own Nifty swing trade and rotating toward growth markets, though he also says investors who trust Nifty should buy more at support. His closing framework: never sit fully in cash because inflation eats it, keep roughly 66% in equities and 33% in stable assets such as bonds and gold bought at supports, and hold 15-20% cash when markets hit all-time highs so dips can be bought. Calls: GOLD BUY (top-up at support, no Rs price stated), GOOGL BUY (buy on dips, no share price stated), NIFTY 50 UNCERTAIN (his own trim versus his buy-at-support advice point in opposite directions). TCS/Infosys discussed only as a possible disruption risk, not recorded as calls.
